title: Identity and n-ary overlay with polymer
text: Identity keeps every part input layer x, split along boundaries identity layer y, attributes . Parts x outside y get missing values y’s attributes, parts y outside x dropped. polymer filter origins piece: keep pieces layer-1 origin, look attributes layer-1 layer-2 features listed pool$layers. function touches polymer’s tables, needs neither ‘sf’ ‘wk’ beyond indexing wk::wkb() vector. Now convert, .
code: identity_pieces <- function(pool, pieces) {   map <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(pieces)), function(i) {     o <- pieces$origins[[i]]     fx <- o$feature[o$layer == 1L]     fy <- o$feature[o$layer == 2L]     if (!length(fx)) return(NULL)        # only in y: dropped     if (!length(fy)) fy <- NA_integer_   # only in x: y attributes missing     expand.grid(piece = i, x = fx, y = fy)   }))   out <- data.frame(pool$layers[[1L]][map$x, , drop = FALSE],                     pool$layers[[2L]][map$y, , drop = FALSE])   rownames(out) <- NULL   out$geometry <- pieces$geometry[map$piece]   out } pool <- polymer(soil_p, field_p) pool #> polymer mesh: #> Layers:    2 #> Features:  14 #> Triangles: 4166 #> Vertices:  2306 (21 at crossings) #> Overlaps:  2224 triangles covered more than once, at most 2 deep ident <- identity_pieces(pool, fuse(pool)) head(ident) #>   soil field #> 1    D     y #> 2    A  <NA> #> 3    E  <NA> #> 4    C     y #> 5    B  <NA> #> 6    A     x #>                                                                                                                    geometry #> 1 <MULTIPOLYGON (((4044330 2942275, 4044160 2942147, 4043615 2941663, 4043392 2941475, 4043216 2941346, 4043014 2941224...> #> 2 <MULTIPOLYGON (((4057798 2939181, 4058361 2939412, 4058083 2941407, 4057571 2941276, 4057531 2941851, 4057564 2941977...> #> 3 <MULTIPOLYGON (((4027533 2979908, 4027765 2979938, 4028097 2980021, 4028200 2980057, 4028313 2980123, 4028411 2980210...> #> 4 <MULTIPOLYGON (((4023563 2962512, 4023482 2962427, 4023253 2961507, 4023258 2960769, 4023701 2960023, 4024480 2959486...> #> 5 <MULTIPOLYGON (((4052867 2955215, 4052886 2954981, 4052905 2954906, 4052957 2954779, 4053099 2954548, 4053270 2954251...> #> 6 <MULTIPOLYGON (((4036969 2990324, 4036981 2989737, 4037004 2989601, 4037104 2989172, 4037345 2989265, 4037461 2989323...> ident <- sf::st_as_sf(ident) plot(ident["field"], main = "soil split by field")

text: workaround issue intersects layers, takes difference x union y, binds two. Written base rbind(): give pieces. Total area per combination soil field values agrees rounding:
code: pairwise_identity <- function(x, y) {   x <- sf::st_set_agr(x, "constant")   y <- sf::st_set_agr(y, "constant")   inter <- sf::st_intersection(x, y)   rest <- sf::st_difference(x, sf::st_union(y))   rest[setdiff(names(y), attr(y, "sf_column"))] <- NA   rest <- sf::st_set_geometry(rest, attr(inter, "sf_column"))   rbind(inter, rest) } base <- pairwise_identity(soil_p, field_p) c(polymer = nrow(ident), pairwise = nrow(base)) #>  polymer pairwise  #>       25       25 key <- function(d) paste(d$soil, d$field) a_poly <- tapply(as.numeric(sf::st_area(ident)), key(ident), sum) a_pair <- tapply(as.numeric(sf::st_area(base)), key(base), sum) range(a_poly / a_pair[names(a_poly)] - 1) #> [1] -6.050715e-13  8.231194e-13

code: tri_area <- function(pool) {   v <- wkpool::pool_vertices(pool$mesh)   t <- wkpool::pool_triangles(pool$mesh)   i <- match(t$.vx0, v$.vx)   j <- match(t$.vx1, v$.vx)   k <- match(t$.vx2, v$.vx)   ((v$x[j] - v$x[i]) * (v$y[k] - v$y[i]) -      (v$x[k] - v$x[i]) * (v$y[j] - v$y[i])) / 2 } ta <- tri_area(pool) idx <- pool$index by_feature <- tapply(ta[idx$triangle], list(idx$layer, idx$feature), sum) range(by_feature[1L, ] / as.numeric(sf::st_area(soil_p)) - 1) #> [1] -7.035483e-13  1.989520e-13

title: Identity and n-ary overlay with polymer
text: Identity one several two-layer overlays GIS software offers side side: Intersect, Union, Identity, Erase Symmetrical Difference. Pairwise clipping computes one separately, geometry. polymer filters pieces, decided whether piece layer-1 origin, layer-2 origin, . mesh built . Pieces covered field polygon filled purple, rest grey.  filter’s area agrees corresponding ‘sf’ operation unioned layers: filters work number layers way. piece’s origins full record covers , rule layers features, “layer 1 layer 3 layer 2”, logical expression table rather sequence clipping operations.
code: pieces <- fuse(pool) in_x <- vapply(pieces$origins, function(o) any(o$layer == 1L), logical(1)) in_y <- vapply(pieces$origins, function(o) any(o$layer == 2L), logical(1)) keep <- list(   intersect = in_x & in_y,   union = in_x | in_y,   identity = in_x,   erase = in_x & !in_y,   symdiff = xor(in_x, in_y) ) op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 5), mar = c(0, 0, 1.5, 0), xaxt = "n", yaxt = "n", bty = "n") for (nm in names(keep)) {   wk::wk_plot(pieces$geometry, border = NA)   title(nm)   wk::wk_plot(pieces$geometry[keep[[nm]]], add = TRUE,               col = c("grey80", "#5142A5")[in_y[keep[[nm]]] + 1L]) } par(op) area <- as.numeric(sf::st_area(sf::st_as_sfc(pieces$geometry))) ux <- sf::st_union(soil_p) uy <- sf::st_union(field_p) sf_area <- function(g) sum(as.numeric(sf::st_area(g))) cbind(polymer = vapply(keep, function(k) sum(area[k]), numeric(1)),       sf = c(sf_area(sf::st_intersection(ux, uy)),              sf_area(sf::st_union(ux, uy)),              sf_area(ux),              sf_area(sf::st_difference(ux, uy)),              sf_area(sf::st_sym_difference(ux, uy)))) #>              polymer         sf #> intersect 1113655938 1113655938 #> union     2893864227 2893864227 #> identity  2564810460 2564810460 #> erase     1451154522 1451154522 #> symdiff   1780208288 1780208288

title: Identity and n-ary overlay with polymer
text: single layer, fuse(polymer(x)) n-ary intersection: one piece per distinct set covering features, count n features origins. example overlapping discs, one disc duplicated, loop posted issue stops duplicate geometries. duplicate needs special handling: discs 1 61 cover triangles, appear together origins every piece inside disc 1. input id column pool$layers, mapping origins ids plain indexing. convert plot overlap count.
code: make_discs <- function(n, seed = 1) {   set.seed(seed)   pts <- sf::st_as_sf(data.frame(x = runif(n, 0, 100), y = runif(n, 0, 100),                                  id = seq_len(n)),                       coords = c("x", "y"))   sf::st_buffer(pts, dist = runif(n, 5, 15), nQuadSegs = 12) } discs <- make_discs(60) discs <- rbind(discs, discs[1, ])  pool <- polymer(discs) pool #> polymer mesh: #> Layers:    1 #> Features:  61 #> Triangles: 5932 #> Vertices:  3268 (388 at crossings) #> Overlaps:  4554 triangles covered more than once, at most 7 deep pieces <- fuse(pool) table(pieces$n) #>  #>   1   2   3   4   5   6   7  #>  47  97 104  72  33  13   3 has_both <- vapply(pieces$origins,                    function(o) all(c(1, 61) %in% o$feature), logical(1)) pieces$origins[[which(has_both)[1L]]] #>   layer feature #> 1     1       1 #> 2     1      19 #> 3     1      25 #> 4     1      61 pieces$ids <- lapply(pieces$origins, function(o) pool$layers[[1L]]$id[o$feature]) nary <- sf::st_as_sf(pieces[c("n", "ids", "geometry")]) plot(nary["n"], main = "overlap count")

title: Identity and n-ary overlay with polymer
text: sf::st_intersection() one layer computes partition. returns one row per piece, can include points, lines collections boundaries touch, polymer returns one MULTIPOLYGON per covering set, rows compare directly. Area per overlap count : pieces partition covered area, two identities hold: area weighted overlap count equals summed area discs, plain area equals area union.
code: sf_nary <- sf::st_intersection(discs) types <- table(sf::st_geometry_type(sf_nary)) types[types > 0] #>  #>              POINT         LINESTRING            POLYGON    MULTILINESTRING  #>                  4                 22                283                 26  #>       MULTIPOLYGON GEOMETRYCOLLECTION  #>                 78                 69  a_poly <- as.numeric(sf::st_area(nary)) rbind(polymer = tapply(a_poly, nary$n, sum),       sf = tapply(as.numeric(sf::st_area(sf_nary)), sf_nary$n.overlaps, sum)) #>                1        2        3        4        5        6        7 #> polymer 3149.089 3115.716 2030.523 878.2377 356.7628 85.49982 10.31411 #> sf      3149.089 3115.716 2030.523 878.2377 356.7628 85.49982 10.31411 c(sum(nary$n * a_poly) / sum(as.numeric(sf::st_area(discs))),   sum(a_poly) / as.numeric(sf::st_area(sf::st_union(discs)))) - 1 #> [1] 2.220446e-16 6.661338e-16

title: Identity and n-ary overlay with polymer
text: reason issue speed. timings recorded (Linux cloud machine, GEOS 3.12.1) rather run vignette built, ‘sf’ call becomes slow number discs grows. small inputs two comparable, Identity example pairwise ‘sf’ route faster. overlaps multiply, cost pairwise clipping grows much faster cost one triangulation. polymer’s time fuse(), rebuilds polygons mesh; mesh index alone, enough counts areas, cheaper still.
code: for (k in c(50, 100, 200)) {   p <- make_discs(k, seed = k)   t_mesh <- system.time(pool <- polymer(p))[["elapsed"]]   t_fuse <- system.time(fuse(pool))[["elapsed"]]   t_sf <- system.time(r <- sf::st_intersection(p))[["elapsed"]]   cat(k, t_mesh, t_mesh + t_fuse, t_sf, nrow(r), nrow(fuse(pool)), "\n") }

code: library(polymer) pool <- polymer(A, B, C) pool #> polymer mesh: #> Layers:    3 #> Features:  6 #> Triangles: 42 #> Vertices:  26 (10 at crossings) #> Overlaps:  15 triangles covered more than once, at most 3 deep head(pool$index) #>   triangle layer feature #> 1        1     1       3 #> 2        1     2       1 #> 3        2     1       1 #> 4        3     1       1 #> 5        4     1       2 #> 6        5     1       4 pieces <- fuse(pool)  ## pieces by the number of features covering them table(pieces$n) #>  #> 1 2 3  #> 4 5 1  ## the deepest piece and the features that make it deepest <- which.max(pieces$n) pieces$geometry[deepest] #> <wk_wkb[1] with CRS=NA> #> [1] <MULTIPOLYGON (((0.2931707 0.63, 0.2502439 0.55, 0.3913934 0.55, 0.347459 0.63, 0.2931707 0.63)))> pieces$origins[[deepest]] #>   layer feature #> 1     1       1 #> 2     2       1 #> 3     3       1  plot(wk::wk_bbox(A), border = NA) wk::wk_plot(pieces$geometry, col = hcl.colors(nrow(pieces)), add = TRUE) plot(pool) wk::wk_plot(layer_n(pool, 2)$geometry, col = "grey", add = TRUE) wk::wk_plot(layer_n(pool, 3)$geometry, col = "dodgerblue", add = TRUE) soil_field <- polymer(soil, field) x <- sf::st_as_sf(layer_n(soil_field, 2)) plot(sf::st_geometry(soil), col = hcl.colors(nrow(soil), "Pastel 1")) plot(sf::st_geometry(x), col = "firebrick", add = TRUE)

text: inputs' edges triangulated together one constrained Delaunay triangulation. edges different features cross, crossing inserted new vertex, mesh partition plane respects every input boundary. title: polymer 0.3.0
text: polymer rebuilt ‘wkpool’ ‘cdtr’. release breaks old interface. polymer now MIT licensed (GPL-3), matching ‘cdtr’ ‘wk’, overlay core can reused freely. New vignette “Identity n-ary overlay polymer” works r-spatial/sf#1959 (Esri Identity) r-spatial/sf#2242 (n-ary intersection one layer), shows Intersect, Union, Identity, Erase Symmetrical Difference filters one mesh, sets ‘sf’ prepares inputs workflow stays polymer’s tables. polymer() takes number layers anything ‘wk’ can read, ‘sf’ data frames. Vertices shared exact coordinate equality ‘wkpool’, edges triangulated ‘cdtr’, inserts crossings new vertices. Triangles now labelled per feature rather per ring, holes subtracted instead counted extra overlap. polymer object holds mesh (‘wkpool’ triangle pool), index (triangle, layer, feature), layers (attributes input) crs. old input, primitives geometry_map elements gone. New fuse() dissolves mesh overlay pieces, one per distinct set covering features, exact partition shared vertices. layer_n() now returns dissolved pieces covered least n times, geometry wk::wkb(), instead one ‘sf’ polygon per triangle. ‘RTriangle’ (non-commercial licence), ‘silicate’, ‘gibble’, ‘sf’ tidyverse packages longer dependencies; ‘sf’ Suggests. %>% re-export removed. soil field data now carry current ‘sf’ crs object. Now use wk geos input handling, output layer_n().
